subject: 48-hour rapid notice: scope, export controls, and runbook alignment
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@finovate.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finovate.com, dpo@finovate.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify 48h notification + evidence/export constraints

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question on the DPA incident notification language — Finovate is reworking our intake runbook and we want to align expectations before our next SOC2 refresh. A couple of points for clarification:

- "48-hour notification": does Redwood commit to initial notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents that meet the DPA threshold? Is that business hours or clock hours?
- Scope: do you treat a compromised customer tenant (data access) the same as a platform service degradation that exposes logs? We need clear examples so we can triage on our side.
- Evidence/exports: if we request a forensic snapshot (logs, request traces, KV cache metadata), what is Redwood's typical turnaround to provide an export? Any constraints on cross-border export or third-party (subprocessor) involvement?
- Subprocessor roster: we'll likely ask for a filtered export showing subprocessor involvement for the impacted keys — is that something you can produce in CSV format?

If you have a short runbook or template for evidence handover, that would help us draft the PoA and internal checklist. We have an internal DPO and legal who may follow up with minimal redlines around export control language.

Thanks — can you confirm by EOD PT?

Best,
Asha Rao
Head of Security, Finovate Payments
asha.rao@finovate.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@finovate.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify 48h notification + evidence/export constraints

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a short runbook (redwood_forensic_runbook_v1.pdf) and a sample subprocessor export layout we can tailor.

- 48 hours: Redwood commits to an initial notification within 48 clock hours of our confirmed detection for incidents that meet the contract's DPA threshold (unauthorized access, exfiltration, or confirmed data exposure). We treat the countdown as clock hours to avoid ambiguity; we'll include timezone in the header of the initial notice.

- Scope examples:
  * Tenant compromise / data exposure (user data exfiltration, unauthorized read) — full notify + forensic scope.
  * System-level log exposure due to misconfiguration — notify + targeted evidence (logs/traces) depending on impact.
  * Service degradation without data access — will trigger an operations alert but not necessarily a DPA-level notification unless evidence shows data exposure.

- Evidence/exports: our standard target is to provide a forensic snapshot manifest within 72 hours of customer request (manifest lists available artifacts). Actual export delivery depends on data volume and legal/export constraints — typical delivery window is 3–10 business days. If expedited transfer is required, we can prioritize but will record the timeline in the runbook.

- Subprocessors: we can produce a filtered CSV tying subprocessors to storage/processing roles for the impacted keys (see attached subprocessor_export_list_20260921.csv). Note: some subprocessors are cloud-hosting partners in jurisdictions with export restrictions; in those cases export may require approvals or redaction.

Exceptions & notes: law-enforcement subpoenas, government orders, or export-control rules can impose additional holds. We'll surface these immediately and propose mitigations (redacted artifact + certified inspector).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the artifacts you need in priority order (e.g., request traces -> S3 object manifests -> compute snapshots).
2) We perform a quick runbook walkthrough (15–30m) with your DPO/legal and our infra/forensics team this week.
3) We run a canned export on a non-prod tenant so both sides verify the CSV and transfer mechanism.

If that works I can loop Monica (legal ops) and Ben (forensics) to set times.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal — Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Folks — forwarding Asha's note and my reply. Action items we need to confirm today:

- Ben: can you confirm we can produce the manifest within 72 hours and a full export in the 3–10 business day range for a typical small-medium incident? Include any tooling constraints (e.g., snapshots that require cold recovery).
- Grace: legal ops / export control — confirm which subprocessors are in restricted jurisdictions and whether we should pre-authorize a mitigation path (redaction + certified third-party reviewer).
- Monica: can you draft a one-paragraph amendment/attachment we can offer customers that clarifies the clock-hours vs business-hours language and sets an expedited fee/process for prioritized exports?

Attachments referenced: redwood_forensic_runbook_v1.pdf, subprocessor_export_list_20260921.csv

Please ack and add timelines. I will share the runbook link with the customer after we align.

Thanks — kim

- Manifest & evidence: manifest delivered target = 72 hours post-request; full export delivery typical range = 3–10 business days (expedite options available).
- Subprocessor exports: we can deliver a contextual CSV tying subprocessors to affected resources; some items may require redaction or approval when crossing export-control boundaries.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) 30-minute walkthrough with your DPO/legal + our Ben (forensics) and Monica (legal ops). Availability: tomorrow 9–11am PT or Thursday 2–4pm PT.
2) We will run a non-prod export exercise and share artifacts via an S3 transfer link (access controlled).
3) Monica will draft the short DPA addendum language that clarifies clock-hour countdown and expedited export process — she'll share the draft in 24 hours.

If that timeline looks OK please reply with preferred slot and the top-three artifacts you want in the manifest (e.g., request traces, object manifests, session cookies/keys). We will treat this as a dry-run; no legal changes required until draft addendum is reviewed.
